transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I guess the main thing that finally got me to make the appointment is… I’m having this issue where someone will be talking to me, especially my wife, and I’ll be looking right at her, like I’m listening, nodding along and everything, but then a minute later I realize I didn’t actually absorb what she said.

A good example is she’ll be telling me about my cousin’s appointments or who needs a ride where, and I’m trying to pay attention, I really am, but then it’s like half of it just didn’t go in. And then I have to ask her again, or I miss something important, and it’s frustrating for both of us. It makes me feel kind of embarrassed, honestly, because I don’t want her thinking I don’t care or I’m ignoring her. That’s really what brought me in.
When did you first start noticing this trouble staying focused on conversations—has it been a lifelong pattern, or is this something that's developed more recently?

I think it’s been around a long time, honestly. It’s not like it just showed up in the last few years. When I think back, even in grade school—definitely before I was 12—teachers would tell my parents things like, “He’s bright, but he’s always daydreaming,” or that I wasn’t finishing my classwork unless someone reminded me.

I remember stuff like leaving homework in my desk instead of bringing it home, and then everyone thinking I just didn’t do it or didn’t care. But it wasn’t that exactly—it was more like I’d lose track of what I was supposed to be doing. So, yeah, the conversation thing is more noticeable now with my wife, but the trouble staying focused feels like it’s been part of me since I was a kid.

Aside from the attention difficulties, have you ever struggled with feeling restless, needing to move around a lot, or acting impulsively—like interrupting others or making quick decisions without thinking them through—either as a child or now?

Hmm… I’m not totally sure how to answer that. I don’t really think of myself as someone who’s been especially restless or impulsive, at least not in the way you’re describing.

Like, I’m not usually jumping out of my seat or feeling like I have to be moving all the time. And I don’t think I’m someone who constantly interrupts people—at least I hope not. My wife might have a more accurate answer there, honestly. I mean, everybody interrupts now and then, but I wouldn’t say that’s been the main issue for me.

As a kid, I don’t remember getting in trouble for being rowdy or hyper or anything like that. If anything, I was probably more the kid who was off in my own head. But with the quick decisions thing… I don’t know. I’d have to think about that more. Nothing really jumps out at me as a big pattern.
Do you notice this same kind of difficulty staying focused or completing tasks at work or in other settings outside of conversations with your wife?

Yes, I do. It’s not just with my wife, though that’s where it probably causes the most obvious friction.

Like, if I sit down to work out a catering order—something where I need to look at the details and make sure the numbers or notes make sense—I’ll start out okay. I’ll think, “Alright, I’ve got this, just go line by line.” But then after a few minutes my mind kind of drifts off without me noticing. I’m still sitting there looking at the paper or the screen, but I’m not really taking it in anymore. Then I’ll realize I don’t remember what I just read, and I have to go back over the same notes again like I never looked at them in the first place.

Same kind of thing happens with parish planning calls. I’ll get on the call and really intend to follow the discussion, especially if there are details about schedules or who’s doing what. But after a while, unless I’m actively writing things down or forcing myself to stay with it, I’ll lose the thread. Then someone will refer back to something that was just said, and I’m thinking, “Wait, when did we decide that?” It’s embarrassing, because I’m not trying to tune out. It just slips away from me.
Have you been experiencing any ongoing sadness, low energy, or excessive worry recently that might be affecting your ability to concentrate?

I’m not sure I’d say that’s been the main thing, no. I mean, I have normal ups and downs like anybody, and I can get frustrated with myself when I realize I missed something or didn’t follow through, but I haven’t really noticed some big ongoing sadness that seems to be driving it.

Low energy… I don’t know. Some days I’m tired, but I don’t have a clear sense that tiredness is what makes me lose focus. It feels more like my mind just wanders even when I’m trying and even when I’m otherwise okay.

And worry—again, I worry about normal things, but I wouldn’t describe it as excessive worry taking over my concentration. At least not that I can tell. It’s more like the concentration problem is there on its own, if that makes sense.
Do you often find yourself losing track of things like keys, paperwork, or your phone, or struggling to keep your workspace and daily tasks organized?

Yes, I do. That one definitely sounds familiar.

It’s usually small things, but it happens all the time—my keys, my phone, receipts from catering orders, even garden clippers if I’ve been outside. I’ll set something down “just for a second,” and then ten minutes later I’m walking around the house trying to reconstruct what I was doing. Like, “Okay, I came in through the kitchen, then I looked at that note on the counter, then maybe I went into the den…” It’s almost like I have to replay the whole scene to figure out where I left it.

The receipts are especially annoying because they’ll be important, and I’ll think I put them somewhere sensible, but then they’re not where I expect them to be. Same with the phone—I’ll put it down while doing something else, and then I’m checking the same two or three places over and over before I finally find it somewhere odd.

I wouldn’t say the house is a total disaster or anything, but keeping track of everyday things and keeping tasks neatly organized is definitely something I struggle with.
